subject: MedLynx DPA redlines & SCCs / transfer addendum — routing and surcharge questions
messages:
From: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@medlynx.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: MedLynx Legal <legal@medlynx.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: MedLynx DPA redlines + transfer addendum (SCCs) — initial pass

Team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our legal team’s initial redline of Redwood’s standard DPA (MedLynx_DPA_redlines_v1.docx). A few priority items where we need confirmation by end of next week: 

- Role delegation: we redlined that MedLynx must be a joint controller for our patient-data ingestion flows; please confirm Redwood’s stance (processor vs joint controller) and any Order Form language that needs to change.
- SCCs vs proposed transfer addendum: since we operate in the EU & UK, our counsel prefers an explicit transfer addendum tying in SCCs + routing controls — is Redwood open to a short addendum (we sketched language in the doc)?
- KMS / key escrow: question about whether keys for encrypted-at-rest content can be customer-managed (we redlined a KMS option).
- Pricing impact: Procurement is asking if enabling regional-only hosting / routing to avoid transfers would incur a surcharge or commitment change. If so, can you provide a ballpark uplift?

Attachments: MedLynx_DPA_redlines_v1.docx

We’re trying to keep procurement on a 2-week cadence for legal signoff. Hoping to identify a path that avoids wholesale redlines but gives our compliance team the evidence they need.

Appreciate a short call if helpful — available Thu 10–12 PT.

Thanks,
Sophie Chen
Senior Counsel, MedLynx Health
Sophie.Chen@medlynx.com

Subject: Re: MedLynx DPA redlines + transfer addendum (SCCs) — initial pass

Folks — looping you in. Quick plan and asks so we can respond to Sophie within 48 hours: 

1) Laura: can you review the redline (attached) for the controller/processor language and the SCCs/transfer addendum suggestion? Flag anything that would require broader MSA/Order Form changes.
2) Security / privacy note: I captured operational asks in DPA_implementation_notes_mina.pdf — we should confirm what evidence we can supply (subprocessor roster, KMS options, region routing SLA).
3) Sales: Ben / Grace — Sophie asked about pricing uplift for region-only routing. Ben, can you prepare a short pricing guidance (ballpark % uplift or per-seat/throughput surcharge) we can share with procurement? We should avoid hard quotes but be responsive.
4) If we can, propose a narrow transfer addendum: (a) tie SCCs to specific hosting regions, (b) optional KMS customer-managed clause, (c) capped surcharge if customer requires strict regional residency. That keeps the MSA unchanged.

I’ll draft the external reply combining legal comments and the implementation note. If Laura wants a call with MedLynx legal, I can schedule Thu 10:30 PT.

-Mina

Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 08:59:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedLynx DPA redlines + transfer addendum (SCCs) — initial pass

Sophie / MedLynx team —

Thanks for the redline. I reviewed the document and attached a focused redline (redline_dpa_mina_v2.docx) with three principal responses:

1) Controller vs Processor: Redwood operates as processor for hosted inference and private deployments unless there is explicit joint data enrichment where Redwood determines business purposes. We can accept clarifying language that confirms Redwood is a processor for the order form scopes described; we cannot accept open-ended joint-controller language. I added a sentence tying scope to the Order Form.

2) SCCs & Transfer Addendum: we are willing to execute a short transfer addendum that references the EU SCCs (and UK addendum) and documents routing constraints. The addendum must: reference specific hosting regions, list mandatory operational controls, and include a fallback for capacity constraints with a permitted routing exceptions process.

3) KMS: we can offer customer-managed keys for on-prem / Private deployments. For Hosted accounts, we provide an option for customer-managed keys via an enterprise KMS integration (subject to technical onboarding and an integration fee). I included a proposed KMS paragraph in the redline.

Pricing / surcharge: I’m not a pricing owner but will not object to designating a bounded surcharge for region-only routing that caps at X% of recurring infra charges — Ben, please fill in the commercial numbers.

Next steps we propose:
- Exchange a short transfer addendum draft (1–2 pages) that ties SCCs to hosting commitments + KMS options.
- We’ll provide subprocessor roster and SOC 2 evidence on request (we prefer a secured link; Mina will send).
- If procurement needs DocuSign, please circulate a PO/DocuSign link and we’ll prioritize the legal review.

Happy to discuss on Thu 10:30 PT — Mina, please schedule if that fits.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: MedLynx DPA redlines + transfer addendum (SCCs) — initial pass

Laura / Mina —

Thanks, that is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The proposed processor language is acceptable to our counsel as long as the Order Form explicitly lists the data ingestion flows that MedLynx controls. We’ll mark that in the draft Order Form.
- KMS: Procurement confirms they’ll accept the enterprise KMS integration option for Hosted, but need an estimate for the integration fee and timeline.
- Pricing: procurement is targeting a single-sourced PO and needs to understand uplift if we require EU-only hosting with guaranteed routing (no fallback to US). We attached a PO (MedLynx_PO.pdf) and a DocuSign link for contracting timeline purposes.

Our timing: procurement would like signed DPA + Order Form within 2 weeks to meet their quarter close. Can Redwood provide: (a) a transfer addendum draft, (b) a short note on the KMS integration cost/time, and (c) a ballpark % uplift for EU-only routing?

DocuSign (Procurement): https://docusign.com/MLX-PO-2028

Best,
Sophie

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MedLynx DPA redlines + transfer addendum (SCCs) — pricing & commercial plan

Team — quick commercial reply so we can respond to procurement: 

- Proposed approach: offer a one-page Transfer Addendum (TAdd) that: references EU & UK SCCs, locks hosting region commitments to EU region(s) listed on the Order Form, provides an operational exceptions process, and includes optional KMS integration.
- Pricing (ballpark): EU-only routing with guaranteed residency (no fallback) would normally be handled as a dedicated-region commitment. For a smaller account like MedLynx we can offer a managed-routing surcharge of 15% on recurring infra charges (min $2,000/mo) or a fixed uplift on GPU throughput pricing. Exact number to be finalized with Finance.
- KMS integration: one-time integration fee estimate: $12k–$25k (depending on vendor), plus 6–8 weeks for onboarding.

Suggested next steps for reply to Sophie: attach the draft TAdd (Laura — can you attach once ready), include the KMS range and the 15% surcharge ballpark, and offer Thu 10:30 PT call to finalize. If procurement needs a DocuSign PO, we’ll prioritize legal signoff on the TAdd + DPA.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

--
Inline proposed Order Form clause (suggested):
"Regional Residency Surcharge: Customer may elect to restrict hosting of Customer Data to the EU region(s) listed on the Order Form. Where Customer elects EU-only residency with no fallback, Customer will pay a Regional Residency Surcharge equal to 15% of recurring infrastructure charges (minimum $2,000/month) for the duration of the residency commitment."
